chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said:

Abu Qurra the hadith narrator asked me to bring him to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him). So I sought permission for that, and he gave me permission. So he entered upon him and asked him about the permissible and the forbidden and the rulings, until his questioning reached tawhid. So Abu Qurra said: We have been narrated that God distributed the Vision and the Speech between two prophets: He distributed the Speech to Moses and the Vision to Muhammad.

So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Who then is the one who conveyed from God to the two communities of jinn and humans that visions cannot comprehend Him [6:103], and they do not encompass Him in knowledge [20:110], and nothing is like Him [42:11]? Was it not Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: How can a man come to all creation and inform them that he came from God and that he is calling them to God by God's command, saying visions cannot comprehend Him, and they do not encompass Him in knowledge, and nothing is like Him, then say: I saw Him with my own eyes and encompassed Him in knowledge and He is in the form of a human? Are you not ashamed? The atheists could not have cast upon him this accusation that he came from God with something, then came with its opposite from another direction.

Abu Qurra said: But He says: And certainly he saw it at another descent [53:13]. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: After this verse is what indicates what he saw, where He says: The heart did not lie about what it saw [53:11] — He is saying the heart of Muhammad did not lie about what his two eyes saw. Then He informed of what he saw, saying: He saw of the greatest signs of his Lord [53:18]. The signs of God are other than God. And God has said: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge [20:110]. So if the visions were to see Him, they would have encompassed Him in knowledge, and recognition would have occurred.

So Abu Qurra said: So you deny the narrations? So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When narrations are in opposition to the Quran, I deny them, and the Muslims have formed consensus that He cannot be encompassed in knowledge, and visions cannot comprehend Him, and nothing is like Him.

key_terms.آيَاتُ رَبِّهِ: Signs of His Lord - the Quranic concept of divine signs distinct from the divine essence
key_terms.التَّوْحِيد: Tawhid - Divine Unity, the doctrine of God's absolute oneness and incomparability
key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْن: The two communities - jinn and humans, addressed by the Prophet's mission
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَة: Vision/sight - the theological question of whether God can be seen by the eyes
key_terms.الزَّنَادِقَة: Atheists/dualists - zanadiqa, those who use contradictions to discredit the Prophet
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَة: Recognition/gnosis - complete knowledge that would follow if vision could truly encompass God

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad see God with his physical eyes according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Ridha (AS) engaged with Abu Qurra, a Sunni hadith scholar, who claimed that God distributed vision to Muhammad and speech to Moses. The Imam refuted this by showing it would create a logical contradiction: the Prophet simultaneously proclaimed God's transcendence while also claiming to have seen Him in human form. The Imam then provided a Quranic interpretation of Surah al-Najm showing Muhammad saw God's signs (ayat), not God Himself, and concluded that any hadith contradicting the Quran's consensus on divine transcendence must be rejected.
